findings.description: list(set(found)) drops the first-found order (and set ordering is arbitrary), contradicting the docstring that says the first query's best match comes first.
The VAT rate is divided by 100 before being passed to apply_vat, which expects a percentage (0-100), so gross is only about 0.2% above net instead of 21%.
Uses > although the field comment says the discount applies to baskets of at least min_basket_cents, so a basket exactly at the minimum gets no discount.
Fields are joined with commas and never quoted, so a city or item text containing a comma or quote breaks the CSV, contradicting the RFC 4180 docstring.
revenue // len(todays) raises ZeroDivisionError on a day with no orders, while the field comment says average should be 0.
Passes page=0 to list_orders, whose pages start at 1, so start = -size and the slice _ORDERS[-size:0] is always empty.
Sorts the list returned by repo.all_orders() in place, which is the repository's own list, so the repo stops being oldest-first and list_orders/first_page return the wrong orders.
locate returns (latitude, longitude) but the code unpacks it as (lon, lat), so zone_for gets swapped coordinates and returns the wrong zone or raises ValueError.
total_weight returns grams, but rate_for expects kilograms, so postage is inflated 1000x and almost every parcel raises FreightRequired.
range(1, attempts) runs only attempts-1 calls; with attempts=1 the function is never called and 'raise None' raises TypeError.
The loop counts business days from start through the day before end, not after start up to and including end; for example Friday to Saturday returns 1 instead of 0.
geocode.locate returns None for an unknown city, so unpacking raises TypeError instead of InvalidOrder, and an out-of-zone city's ValueError from zone_for is also not turned into InvalidOrder.
